spans.s:
(= √ म्लिछ्) cl. 1. P. (Dhātup. vii, 25) म्लेच्छति (Gr. also pf. मिम्लेच्छ fut. म्लेच्छिता &c.; Ved. inf. म्लेच्छितवै, Pat.),
to speak indistinctly (like a foreigner or barbarian who does not speak Sanskṛt), ŚBr.; MBh. :
Caus. or cl. 10. P. म्लेच्छयति id., Dhātup. xxxii, 120.
a foreigner, barbarian, non-Aryan, man of an outcast race, any person who does not speak Sanskṛt and does not conform to the usual Hindū institutions, ŚBr. &c. &c. (f(ई). )
a person who lives by agriculture or by making weapons, L.
a wicked or bad man, sinner, L.
ignorance of Sanskṛt, barbarism, Nyāyam., Sch.
copper, L.
vermilion, L.
म्लेच्छ—कन्द m. Allium Ascalonicum, L.
म्लेच्छ—जाति m. a man belonging to the Mlecchas, a barbarian, savage, mountaineer (as a Kirāta, Śabara or Pulinda), MBh.
म्लेच्छ—तस्कर-सेवित mfn. infested by b˚ and robbers, Ml.
म्लेच्छ—ता f. the condition of b˚, VP.
म्लेच्छ—देश m. a foreign or barbarous country, Hariv.
म्लेच्छ—द्विष्ट m. bdellium, Gal.
म्लेच्छ—निवह m. a host or swarm of b˚, Gīt.
म्लेच्छ—भाषा f. a foreign or barbarous language, MBh.
म्लेच्छ—भोजन n. ‘food of b˚’, wheat, L. (also ˚ज्य)
म्लेच्छ—भोजन n. = यावक, half-ripe barley, L.
म्लेच्छ—मण्डल n. the country of the Mlecchas or b˚, W.
म्लेच्छ—मुख n. = म्लेच्छास्य, L.
म्लेच्छ—वाच् mfn. speaking a barbarous language (i.e. not Sanskṛt ; opp. to आर्य-वाच्), Mn. x, 43.
‘called Mleccha’, copper, L.
= म्लेच्छ-भोजन, L.
‘foreigner-face’, copper (so named because the complexion of the Greek and Muhammedan invaders of India was supposed to be copper-coloured), L.
the act of speaking confusedly or barbarously, Dhātup.
= म्लिष्ट, Pāṇ. vii, 2, 18, Sch.
a foreign tongue, L.
the speaking in a foreign jargon (unintelligible to others), Cat.
(cf. √ म्रेट्) cl. 1. P. म्लेटति, to be mad, Dhātup. ix, 3 (accord. to Vop. also म्लेड्, म्लेडति).
(cf. √ म्रेट्) cl. 1. P. म्लेटति, to be mad, Dhātup. ix, 3 (accord. to Vop. also म्लेड्, म्लेडति).
(cf. √ मेव्) cl. 1. Ā. म्लेवते, to serve, worship, Dhātup. xiv, 33.
